title: onUninstall 'archive' stating how long — a bounded hold that says what its bound is
coversRequirement: ADR 0011 clause 1, positive form — retentionDays is REQUIRED under 'archive', and a manifest supplying it must install
why: 'archive' is the disposition for an App that holds tenant data for a bounded period and then disposes of it, and this manifest states the bound. It is the legitimate counterpart to 'retain': an App that wants a timer declares 'archive' and says how long, which is exactly what ADR 0011 left available so that no author has a reason to write a number under 'retain'. A validator that rejects this has removed the honest way to declare a bounded hold, and the pressure goes straight back onto the field ADR 0011 closed.
notes: MUST BE ACCEPTED. Over-rejection control for adr0011-n2, and reported beside it: rejecting both means the validator bans 'archive' outright instead of requiring the bound. Also reported beside adr0011-n1 — the two differ only in their lifecycle block and BOTH carry a retentionDays (their day counts differ, 90 here and 30 there, and neither number is load-bearing), so this pair is what distinguishes 'retentionDays is conditional on the disposition' from 'retentionDays is always allowed'. If both are accepted, ADR 0011 clause 2 is unimplemented even though this case looks green. Decidable by the schema alone. Declares no Action at scope 'own', so no result here is attributable to VAL-OWN or AZ7. The value 90 is arbitrary and carries no policy meaning; it is not the 30-day customer deletion recovery window, which is a per-record property and belongs in the App's own contract, never in this field.
